clue.text: Decline food served up with squashed fly

indicators.note: the fly is squashed into the middle of the upturned food word
in a down clue, served up means the word is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: eats is an informal word for food
a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a plate of food once they spot a squashed fly on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse; it means wane. 'served up' gives STAE, and 'squashed' presses the fly into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop developing and so decline or go stale.

clue.text: See 24 across
Film about sport, Alpine challenge

indicators.note: about means the film word goes round the sport abbreviation

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer over something
RU is short for rugby union, a sport

explanation.surface: A film about a sport, perhaps an Alpine adventure documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski slope in the Alps is a downhill course that tests a skier.

clue.text: Block leftists finally in Tory gain

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, i.e. Tory

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the Tory gain pair

parts.note: to gain is to get

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of leftists

explanation.surface: Leftist votes at the end of the count deny the Tories a gain.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for Conservative is the usual crossword shorthand for a Tory; 'in' sets the picked letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To congest a road or passage is to clog or obstruct it.

clue.text: Sliced food, shortcake could I be?

parts.note: read as short cake: pastry with its last letter cut off
the question could I be? is answered by am I

explanation.surface: A piece of shortcake wonders whether it might be some sliced food.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortcake is a biscuit, in keeping with the puzzle's biscuit theme; split it as 'short cake' to give PASTR(Y).
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, smoked beef usually served thinly sliced in sandwiches.

clue.text: Wash organ munching old biscuit

indicators.note: munching means the wash and organ pair take the old letter into their mouth

parts.note: to bath is to wash
the liver is a body organ

explanation.surface: An organ, freshly washed, munches an old biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is a plain dry cracker-like biscuit first made in the city of Bath.

clue.text: Coarse part of biscuit?

indicators.note: part of means only some of the biscuit's letters are kept, the middle stretch

parts.note: a garibaldi is a currant biscuit

explanation.surface: Asks whether something coarse is a piece of biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside GARIBALDI, a British biscuit with squashed currants, but the biscuit's name is not printed, so it is a trimmed synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is vulgar and indecent, which is coarse.

clue.text: Doctor is OK keeping lean, probably

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the lean word inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: lean means thin

explanation.surface: A doctor says a patient is fine while keeping them thin, probably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges IS OK into IKSO, which 'keeping' wraps around THIN after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedged yes, used when something is likely but not certain.

clue.text: Soak leaving biscuits for musical family

indicators.note: leaving means the soak word departs from the biscuits word

parts.note: amaretti are Italian almond biscuits
to ret is to soak flax or hemp

explanation.surface: Someone stops soaking biscuits, for a musical family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amatis of Cremona were a famous dynasty of violin makers.

clue.text: Monster so revolting or repulsive, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A monster described as so revolting or repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like a reversal signal, but the four last letters of so, revolting, or, repulsive spell the answer directly.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore an ogre is a man-eating giant, a classic monster.

clue.text: A tad higher, crackers in front of you

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crackers placed a little higher, there in front of you.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers are also biscuits, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something straight before you, directly forward, is in front of you.

clue.text: Accountant has left biscuit, 15

indicators.note: has left means the accountant has departed from the biscuit

parts.note: a macaroon is an almond or coconut biscuit
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant has walked off leaving a biscuit behind.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' refers to the answer at 15 across, a shade of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a dark brownish-crimson colour, a deep red shade.

clue.text: Labour currently in workplace?

definitions.meaning: the Labour Party was then the main party out of government in Britain
the place one holds when at work, op being work

explanation.surface: Wonders whether today's Labour party is at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The party out of power forms the official parliamentary group that challenges government.

clue.text: Minor notices sons poaching duck: that's not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is dropped
poaching means the sons take the duck in, enclosing it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons give two S letters
a mallard is a duck

explanation.surface: Local notices report sons poaching a duck, which is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified advertisements in a newspaper are short, small-print announcements.

clue.text: Shade found parking between river and sea

indicators.note: between puts the parking letter in the gap between river and sea

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A shady parking spot found between a river and the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich dark crimson is one colour, i.e. a shade of red.

clue.text: Condemn cost of employing manager?

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a manager
a rate is the cost or fee charged for hiring someone

explanation.surface: Asks what it costs to hire a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or curse something as detestable.

clue.text: Short shelf, so shiny and grey

indicators.note: short means the shelf word loses its last letter

parts.note: a sill is a ledge or shelf under a window
so, as in so good, means very

explanation.surface: A short shelf, so shiny and grey, perhaps in steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvery describes the lustrous pale grey of the metal silver.

clue.text: Biscuit inspiring uprising in country, tempt fate

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the biscuit takes the country inside

parts.note: a rusk is a hard dry biscuit

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the country is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A biscuit inspires an uprising in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' gives NARI, which 'inspiring' (breathing in) draws into the biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a chance with danger is to tempt fate.

clue.text: Plant grains, scattered round bottom of driveway

indicators.note: round means the rearranged grains surround that last letter
scattered grains are thrown about, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Plant grains scattered round the end of a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges GRAINS into SRINGA, placed 'round' Y as SYRINGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus of lilac, also a name for mock orange.

clue.text: Unshaven redhead tucked into bourbon

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the bourbon word

parts.note: bourbon is an American whiskey
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A scruffy redhead tucking into bourbon.
explanation.walkthrough: A bourbon is also a British chocolate biscuit, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskery means having bristles or stubble on the face, as an unshaven person does.

clue.text: Torment two animals, the first tailless

indicators.note: the first animal loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: a hare and an ass are two animals

explanation.surface: Torment two animals, the first having lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to pester or persecute persistently.

clue.text: 12 fibre

definitions.meaning: the answer to 12, i.e. to leave someone ...

explanation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to leave them stuck, and a thread of fibre is a filament.

clue.text: Beautiful second cake without filling, almost delightful

indicators.note: the middle letters of cake are removed, leaving its outer pair

parts.note: the word cake taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, losing its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant or delightful

explanation.surface: A second slice of cake without filling is almost delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic views are picturesque, pretty to look at.

clue.text: Winger breaking Cantona's strawberry hobnob

indicators.note: breaking means the bird splits the strawberry word apart

parts.note: Eric Cantona is French, and fraise is French for strawberry
a tern is a bird, i.e. a winger

explanation.surface: A winger muscles into Cantona's strawberry hobnob, like a football anecdote.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantona was a French footballer, so 'Winger' feels like a football position; here it is a bird. A hobnob is also a British oat biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, to be friendly with others.

clue.text: Kid with tribe's written off vehicle

indicators.note: a car written off is wrecked, so these letters are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word tribe, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A kid and his tribe crash a vehicle so badly that it is written off.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-road motorcycle built for rough tracks is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Timeless Florentine writer, European

indicators.note: timeless means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was a poet from Florence

explanation.surface: A Florentine writer described as timeless and European.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Denmark is a European.

clue.text: Large drink …

explanation.definitionFit: A stout person is portly, and a stout is a dark porter-style beer.

clue.text: … for which bar charges suspect

indicators.note: charges means rushes in, so the bar goes inside the suspect word

parts.note: to suspect is to guess
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: Continuing 25: a drink for which a suspicious bar charges too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 25: 'for which' points to the drink, stout, of which this is the best-known brand.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish brand is the most famous example of a dark stout beer.
